editorial:
Two hundred years after Dr. Frankenstein brought him to life, his creature Adam is still wandering the earth. He looks like a tough, scarred fighter, and he has spent centuries staying out of trouble. That changes when he gets pulled into a secret war between good gargoyles and evil demons. The demons want the secrets of reanimation so they can bring an army of corpses to life and take over the world. Adam holds the key, and suddenly everyone wants him on their side. The movie has a dark, gothic look and lots of action, but the story feels rushed and a bit silly.

Aaron Eckhart gives it his all as Adam, and Bill Nighy is fun as the villain. The fight scenes are fast and flashy, though the special effects look cheap in places. The biggest problem is the weak script and flat characters, which make it hard to care about what happens. If you enjoy mindless action and monster movies, you might have a decent time. For most viewers, though, this one is a skip. You can stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent it on Apple TV, or grab the 4K Blu-ray if you are a collector.
endingExplained: In the final battle, Adam confronts the demon prince Naberius inside the cathedral. Using the secrets of reanimation against him, Adam destroys Naberius and sends the demons back to hell. The gargoyles accept Adam as an ally. Adam then walks into the city, vowing to protect humanity from hidden threats. The twist is that the monster finally claims his creator's name, declaring himself Frankenstein.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves mindless monster action and gothic fantasy.
